guide.title: Quarry Road: Waterville's rope tow, on the site of the old Colby Ski Area
guide.intro: Quarry Road Trails, per its own homepage, "is owned and operated by the City of Waterville Department of Parks & Recreation." Alongside its Nordic trail network, the operator's own "Rope Tow Ski Hill" page states, "In December 2021, we installed a rope tow at the base of the former Colby Ski Area," serving "the lower portion of the historical ski slope," run by "Friends of Quarry Road and Waterville Parks and Recreation," with Friends of Quarry Road described on the same page as "a 501(c)(3) nonprofit." For the 2026-27 season, per the same page, the alpine rope tow is "Open 4 days a week for lift-served Skiing: Dec. 27- Mar. 15," the sixth year of the rope tow's operation, with hours of Wednesdays and Fridays 3pm-7pm and Saturdays and Sundays 10am-2pm.

sections.heading: The historical Colby Ski Area, 1938 to the 1970s energy crisis
sections.body: Per Quarry Road's own "Rope Tow Ski Hill" page, the site's first lift was a 1,200-foot rope tow that opened to the public in January 1938, on a slope "known initially as Dunham's Mountain Farm and later the Colby Ski Area." Per the operator's own "History" page, the area's history began "in the 1930's with a tow rope," and it became "a hub of activity for local ski enthusiasts." The hill was closed during World War II, then re-opened by veterans and the Colby Outing Club in the late 1940s. It operated again "in the late 60's/early 70's when operated by Colby College as a lighted ski area with limited snowmaking," per the same page; downhill operations were then suspended specifically "during the 1970s energy crisis," per the "Rope Tow Ski Hill" page, and "the area closed again and was abandoned for a number of years," per the "History" page. At its peak, per the operator's own site, "the 250-foot hill featured a T-bar, snowmaking, lights for night skiing, and a spacious lodge."

sections.heading: Revival: 2007 to today's rope tow
sections.body: In 2007, per Quarry Road's own "History" page, "a small group of volunteers gathered to revive outdoor recreation once again at Quarry Road," developing a year-round recreation area with the City of Waterville. In February 2021, per the operator's own "Rope Tow Ski Hill" page, "we ran a snowmobile-assisted alpine ski day" on the old slope, ahead of the rope tow's December 2021 installation. For 2026-2027, per the operator's own "Ski Ticket & Pass Rates" page, alpine season passes are $80 (adult 19-64), $60 (student 7-18 or senior 65+), and $200 (family of 2 adults + 2 students), with discounted rates for Waterville residents. Friends of Quarry Road states it has "raised over $120,000 for bringing lift-served skiing back to Waterville" toward a future capital plan for "new lift infrastructure, snowmaking, a permanent base lodge / outdoor center," per the operator's own page, crediting a challenge gift from the Bill and Joan Alfond Foundation and lead donors Golden Pond Wealth Management and Ned and Erica Ervin. The Quarry Road Ski Club also runs an "introductory alpine skiing program for area youth in grades 2-8" using the rope tow, per the Club's own site, in two 4-week sessions costing $65 for the 2025-26 season.

sections.heading: In Waterville
sections.body: The Colby College Museum of Art, per the college's own "Visit" page, sits on the Colby College campus at "5600 Mayflower Hill Dr. Waterville, ME 04901." The Redington Museum, operated by the Waterville Historical Society, is housed in "an elegant Federal-style home that was built by Asa Redington in 1814," per the Society's own site. The Waterville Opera House, at 1 Common Street, is a performing-arts venue that, per Waterville Creates' own capital-campaign materials, is now connected by "a new skywalk that will provide an accessible connection" to the Waterville Opera House lobby from the newly built Paul J. Schupf Art Center. The Maine Film Center, per Waterville Creates' own "About Us" page, "educates, entertains, and builds community through film," operating Railroad Square Cinema's three screening rooms, now relocated into the Art Center at 93 Main Street, which opened to the public December 17, 2022. Front & Main, at 9 Main Street, describes itself, per its own website, as offering "Creative, nourishing cuisine, sourced lovingly from our own farms, fields, bays and oceans." Per Wikipedia's "Waterville, Maine" article, "The $26 million Lockwood Hotel...opened in August 2022 as downtown's first new hotel in over a century," a 53-room hotel developed by Colby College and managed by Charlestowne Hotels, housing the Front & Main restaurant.

faq.question: Is Quarry Road a lift-served ski area or just a Nordic trail center?
faq.answer: Both: it is primarily a Nordic trail network, but per the operator's own "Rope Tow Ski Hill" page, a rope tow installed in December 2021 serves the lower portion of the historic Colby Ski Area slope, open four days a week for the 2026-27 season.

faq.question: What was at Quarry Road before the current rope tow?
faq.answer: The Colby Ski Area, whose first lift, per the operator's own site, was a 1,200-foot rope tow that opened to the public in January 1938; it operated in phases through World War II, the Colby College era of the late 1960s and early 1970s, and a shutdown "during the 1970s energy crisis," before the site's broader revival beginning in 2007.

places.name: Colby College Museum of Art
places.summary: An art museum on the Colby College campus in Waterville.
places.history: Per the college's own museum "Visit" page, the Colby College Museum of Art is located on the Colby College campus in Waterville, at 5600 Mayflower Hill Dr., corroborated by Wikipedia's Colby College Museum of Art article.

places.name: Redington Museum
places.summary: A Waterville history museum operated by the Waterville Historical Society, housed in an 1814 Federal-style home.
places.history: Per the Waterville Historical Society's own site, the Redington Museum is housed in "an elegant Federal-style home that was built by Asa Redington in 1814," offering "a comprehensive and charming view of life in Waterville during the past two centuries" through collections of furniture, household artifacts, and historical papers.

places.name: Waterville Opera House
places.summary: A downtown Waterville performing-arts venue, now skywalk-connected to the Paul J. Schupf Art Center.
places.history: Per Waterville Creates' own contact page, the Waterville Opera House's address is 1 Common Street, Waterville. Per the organization's own capital-campaign materials, "a new skywalk that will provide an accessible connection to the Waterville Opera House lobby" now joins it to the newly built Paul J. Schupf Art Center, indicating the Opera House remains a separate, physically connected building.

places.name: Maine Film Center (Railroad Square Cinema)
places.summary: A film nonprofit operating Railroad Square Cinema's three screening rooms, relocated in 2022 into the Paul J. Schupf Art Center.
places.history: Per Waterville Creates' own "About Us" page, the Maine Film Center "educates, entertains, and builds community through film," operating "Railroad Square Cinema (three digital projection theaters)" and presenting the annual Maine International Film Festival; its screening rooms are now part of the Paul J. Schupf Art Center at 93 Main Street, which opened to the public December 17, 2022.

places.name: Front & Main
places.summary: An upscale downtown Waterville restaurant housed inside the Lockwood Hotel.
places.history: Per its own website, Front & Main describes its food as "Creative, nourishing cuisine, sourced lovingly from our own farms, fields, bays and oceans," with "a great wine list" and private dining options.

places.name: Lockwood Hotel
places.summary: A 53-room downtown Waterville hotel developed by Colby College, opened in 2022.
places.history: Per Wikipedia's "Waterville, Maine" article, "The $26 million Lockwood Hotel...opened in August 2022 as downtown's first new hotel in over a century. The 53-room hotel, developed by Colby College and managed by Charlestowne Hotels, features the Front & Main restaurant."
